newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander up on management changes talk.
newsitem.headline: Santander up on management changes talk.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Banco Santander were sharply higher on Wednesday amid market talk of key management changes, analysts said.
At 1350 GMT, Santander was up 150 pesetas at 9,910, while the Ibex was up 0.19 percent at 5,515.98.
Santander's recent choice of Francisco Luzon -- former head of Argentaria -- as a joint general director to work alongside chairman Emilio Botin is at the hub of the rumours.
There are expectations that Luzon will be named CEO of the bank at the next shareholders' meeting, analysts said.
"Luzon is the perfect person to shake up the branch network. He's a good manager," one banking analyst said.
Analysts are to meet representative of the bank on March 18, and this could provide details of any changes planned.

The Santander group has shown strong growth in the past few years, but now it needs to cut costs and clarify its relationship with Banco Espanol de Credito (Banesto), in which it has a 53 percent stake, they said.
Banesto's share price climbed sharply at the end of last year and the start of 1997, also buoyed by talk of management shuffles. But this was one of a number of rumours circulating.

"There's a lot of spare capacity (between Santander and Banesto) and they need to apply the best of each. Furthermore, they need to reduce their central services," a second analyst said, requesting anonymity.
Luzon would carry out the rationalisation of the group, giving it a basis for solid growth.
"The bank can still benefit this year from lower interest rates, some asset sales and, above all, from the dollar's rise, but the retail banking side has to grow," an analyst said.
A spokesman for Santander said Luzon's arrival at the bank in November was due to commercial as well as corporate strategies. He declined to comment further.
Another factor fuelling the stock is the fact that banks are in vogue, backed by broker recommendations.
"Banks are hot property at the moment, with major brokerages upgrading recommendations in Spain," a trader said.
Since January 2 the stock has climbed from 8,090 pesetas, or around 18 percent.
